assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's one curated REVIEWED item at basis_commit: COTE_CHAR_LEDGER_RIVALS_LEADERS_THROUGH_Y2.md (89,913 bytes, status canonical, veto false), a shared rival-leader character ledger over the frozen Year 1 V2 conclusion, canonical Y2V01-Y2V12.5, Volume 0 at its mandated retrospective position and the Year 2 guidebook Second List, with Year-3 evidence excluded. The evaluator read in full its front matter and boundary notice, the ledger function and comparative thesis (sections 0-1) and Ryuen's individual section 2 (lines 83-252), the part the row enrolls; the Ichinose, Sakayanagi, Koenji and Nagumo sections were not used. The section locates claims by volume and routes each to a canonical deep reading; it quotes no Ryuen line and gives no page locator. The Y2 deep readings, the class-polity ledger and the cross-cast behavioral reconstruction protocol it names or that exist beside it are not curated on this subject, and no claim rests on them. The evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Year-2 states from Y2V01 through the Second List boundary (Y2SL), at the ledger's volume resolution: V01 adaptive post-defeat state; V02 Katsuragi recruitment; V04 Hosen confrontation and delegation; V04.5 Komiya testimony and injury visit; V05 managed intimidation of Tokito that leaves him a route to stay; V06-V07 Horikita contracts and staged festival rivalry; V09 failed Ichinose model and update; V10 win through the Hashimoto irregularity and Hiyori's dependence warning; V11 coercion of Tokito; V12 merit loss to Sakayanagi; V12.5 refusal of the official victory and Sakayanagi's departure. Year 1 enters only as the frozen baseline (the rooftop defeat and voluntary preservation). Y2V03 and Y2V08 have no row in the ledger's progression table. No Year-3 state.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, applying the owner calibration rulings recorded there (B/C boundary, single counting of uncertainty, dialogue constrained-use test, chronology splits, relationship-transfer safeguards and control-state attribution); evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The ledger names his governing drives with located support: sovereignty kept through coercion, threat and asymmetric information (2.3 CONFIRMED_CONTINUITY); respect earned by nerve, useful dissent and demonstrated competence; and a late meaningful-victory standard in which a win must authenticate the person he has become (V12.5, 2.2). It gives eight modeling tendencies, some with conditions: coercion when he believes it preserves sovereignty or exposes weakness, delegation when a subordinate has a differentiated skill, revision when evidence shows the opponent changed (2.5). Not B: the tendencies are unordered, and the ledger leaves open what triggers escalation from managed intimidation that leaves a dissenter a route to stay (V05: threats and humiliation, no purge) to physical coercion and threatened pursuit (V11) and whether Hiyori's correction can bind him (Y1H-025 PARTIALLY_ANSWERED, Y1H-026 STILL_OPEN). Not D: the drives are specific, located by volume and stated with conditions.

The strongest dimension. A frozen Year-1 baseline (2.1), a positive progression and a simultaneous negative continuity (2.2), changes classified as continuity, development, revelation, recontextualization, correction and relationship-specific expression (2.3), and a twelve-position volume table from Y2V01 to Y2SL that gives each delta its reason and canonical route (2.4): Katsuragi recruited for expertise his polity lacks (V02), the threat model revised after the V09 failure, the official result refused at V12.5. Not A: states are located by volume only, Year 1 is one summarized baseline, and Y2V03 and Y2V08 have no row. Not C: the ledger traces state change with reasons and keeps the persistent authoritarian jurisdiction beside the development.

The row claims no SPEECH dimension, and section 2 analyzes no register, address form or line; it quotes nothing he says. Threats, humiliation and mockery of Tokito are named as acts (V05, V11), not as voice. Nothing is established, so no grade is given.

Section 2 reads his conduct as a class leader. Its only act outside competition is the injury visit to Komiya (V04.5), which the ledger uses as evidence of follower legitimacy. Ordinary life is not analyzed, so no grade is given.

Partner-specific expression is listed with located support (2.3): Ayanokoji as desired rival and benchmark; Katsuragi valued for being different from him (V02, V04); Hiyori as diagnostician whose influence is respected but not binding (V10); Ishizaki, Albert and Komiya as loyalty that survives defeat (V04, V04.5); Tokito as the dissent stress test (V05, V11); Sakayanagi as the rival whose loss matters relationally (V12.5); Horikita as a contract partner (V06-V07). Not B: the entries describe what each relation is, not how his conduct changes in a new situation with that partner, and the Tokito case shows the same partner meeting managed intimidation that leaves a route to stay (V05) and physical coercion with threatened pursuit (V11) without a stated trigger for the escalation. Not D: the differences are located and partly explained.

Inner states are almost all inferred from conduct: that he refuses to treat the V12.5 result as the victory he wanted, that Sakayanagi's disappearance matters to him relationally, and that he is more attached to rivals and followers than his early fear theory admits (2.2, 2.5). The ledger's function is political comparison (section 0), and it draws no account of his inner life. Not D: the items are few and come from the analyst's reading of his acts.

His conflict repertoire is the ledger's core and is located: the V01 pairing market turned into a price and intelligence field; the V04 Hosen fight redefined so that the alarm, Katsuragi's exam duties and not sacrificing Ishizaki and Albert decide the win; false YES votes to expose the V05 dissenter, then threats and humiliation that still leave him a route to stay; V06 written contracts; V09 sabotage, then an updated threat model; the V11 physical coercion of Tokito. Tendencies: adversarial interpretation by default, exploitation of rule gaps, traitors and miscalibration, and coercion when he believes it preserves sovereignty (2.3, 2.5). Not B: for conflict inside his own class, the ledger does not say what triggers escalation from managed intimidation to physical coercion and threatened pursuit, and calls V11 a negative control rather than explaining it. Not D: the inter-class repertoire recurs with located outcomes and stated conditions.

Value-relevant acts are located across the year: not sacrificing followers to his pride (V04), the visit to the injured Komiya (V04.5), threatening and humiliating Tokito while leaving him a route to stay (V05) and then coercing him physically (V11), and refusing a victory he did not earn (V12.5). The ledger reads them as real but non-redemptive development and separates sociological from ethical legitimacy (sections 0, 2.2, 2.3). Not C: no deliberation of his own is shown, and the ledger leaves moral redirection of him explicitly open (Y1H-026). Not E: the acts span several volumes and are read coherently.
Section 2 does not analyze humor or play. Staged festival rivalry (V07) is read as strategy. Nothing is established, so no grade is given.

One 170-line section of a shared comparative ledger, built on a Japanese-primary Year-2 corpus and routed volume by volume to canonical readings. Not C: the section's purpose is leadership function (section 0), it quotes no line and gives no page locator, Year 1 is inherited as a summary, two Year-2 volumes have no row, and speech, ordinary life and interiority are outside it. Not E: every Year-2 position it lists is routed to a canonical reading, and the Second List measurement is cited by entry (Y2SL-E029-E036).

The ledger affirmatively blocks several readings with located evidence: defeat did not reform him into a benevolent leader (Tokito, V05 and V11); followers do not stay only from fear (V04.5); his strength is not brute improvisation (Katsuragi, contracts, delegation, V09 update); Hiyori has no demonstrated veto; the corpus does not establish White Room genealogy for his method (2.3); the E+ social-contribution score is not low social causality (2.5); and a list of modeling errors to avoid. Not A: it states where each reading fails without explaining every boundary. Not C: these are located findings, not inferences from silence.

Every Year-2 claim is placed by volume, and V12 (merit loss) is kept apart from V12.5 (refusal of the official result). Not B: there is no within-volume location, Year 1 is one baseline, and Y2V03 and Y2V08 are unplaced. Not D: the volume placement is explicit and consistent across sections 2.2-2.4.

scenario_readiness.note: Not assessed: the curated section analyzes no speech and quotes no line, and the row claims no SPEECH dimension. Silence is not read as a finding about his voice.

conditions: Chronology is one named Year-2 state at the ledger's volume resolution, defaulting to Y2SL (after Sakayanagi's departure). Pre-V02 states have no Katsuragi; pre-V12.5 states have Sakayanagi as an active rival.

The interlocutor is a sampled relation in its recorded state: Ayanokoji, Katsuragi, Hiyori, Ishizaki, Albert, Komiya, Tokito, Horikita as contract partner, Sakayanagi, Hosen or Ichinose's class as opponents. Transfer to an unsampled classmate or rival is a separate, lower-confidence condition that uses the stated tendencies without invented history.
Output strategic choice families (pressure, information play, recruitment, contract, delegation, model update, refusal of a hollow win), not exact speech or affect.

When a member of his own class dissents openly, whether he stops at managed intimidation that leaves the dissenter a route to stay (V05: threats and humiliation, no purge) or escalates to physical coercion and threatened pursuit (V11) is output as an open fork; the trigger for escalation is not established. Hiyori's criticism may influence him but is never treated as a binding veto.
Neither redemption nor a purely violent caricature: coercion and voluntary loyalty stay simultaneous (2.5 errors to avoid).

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One named Year-2 state from Y2V01 to Y2SL, defaulting to Y2SL; Year 1 only as the frozen baseline; no Year-3 events.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Sampled relations in their recorded state: Ayanokoji as desired rival, Katsuragi as valued differentiated subordinate, Hiyori as respected non-binding critic, Ishizaki, Albert and Komiya as voluntary followers, Tokito as open dissenter, Horikita as contract partner, Sakayanagi as rival, Hosen and Ichinose's class as opponents; an unsampled person only at lower confidence.
setting_constraints: Advanced Nurturing High School: class competition, special examinations, OAA and class points
No adult, occupational or post-graduation setting
Internal-dissent outcomes end in an open fork

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded counterfactuals inside the school's competitive setting with sampled interlocutors; outcomes inside his own class's dissent are open forks.
Not assessed: the section reads only his leadership and rivalry; the Komiya visit is its one non-competitive act. Silence is not read as a finding about his ordinary social life.

The evidence affirmatively bounds this domain: it calls his development non-redemptive, records moral redirection of him as STILL_OPEN (Y1H-026) and warns against modeling it as redemption. It shows value-relevant acts but no deliberation, so a scenario that needs him to weigh an ethical choice would invent the decisive step.
Not assessed: the section contains no romantic material. Silence is not a finding.

conditions: School-institutional leadership only: special examinations, the pairing and OAA economy, class-point competition, inter-class contracts and festival competition (V01-V12.5).

He recruits a differentiated skill, delegates bounded domains and revises a failed model; his class's dependence on his judgment is the standing risk Hiyori and the Second List review name (V10, Y2SL).
scenario_readiness.note: Read as his class-leader role in the school's competitive institutions; no occupational evidence exists.

known_limits.statement: What triggers escalation from managed intimidation (V05: threats and humiliation that leave Tokito a route to stay) to physical coercion and threatened pursuit (V11) is not explained; the ledger treats V11 as a negative control, and protected dissent remains absent (Y1H-025 PARTIALLY_ANSWERED).
Hiyori is a valued corrective voice without demonstrated veto authority; moral redirection of Ryuen is STILL_OPEN (Y1H-026).
Greater legitimacy and sophistication coexist with persistent coercive jurisdiction; follower loyalty does not prove coercion disappeared, and coercion does not prove loyalty fake.

The Second List file is not a total character ontology: the official profile says his leadership and strategy exceed the axes, and the E+ social-contribution score is not low social causality (Y2SL-E030-E031).

Comparison of his environmental intimidation with Year-2 authored-choice themes is structural only; the corpus does not establish White Room genealogy or Atsuomi-like preference engineering for his method.
The curated section analyzes no speech, register or address form and quotes no line; any generated speech would be constrained by strategy content only.
Ordinary life, humor and play, and romance are not covered by the curated section.
Claims are located by volume only, with no page or line locator; Year 1 is one summarized baseline; Y2V03 and Y2V08 have no row in the progression table.

The per-volume Y2 deep readings, the class-polity ledger and the cross-cast behavioral reconstruction protocol on main are not curated on this subject; no claim rests on them, and their content may refine or contradict this assessment.
The ledger excludes Year 3; nothing here bounds his conduct after Y2SL.
